plot.title: Web of Finance
plot.setup: Spider-Man needs to fix his web-shooters (a costly repair!) while fighting the Vulture, who is stealing tech from Stark Industries.
plot.location: A bustling street in downtown Manhattan, with a damaged bank (from a previous supervillain fight) visible in the background. Stark Tower looms in the distance.

dialogue.text: Alright, Spidey, you alright? Your web-shooters went offline mid-fight! Listen, your web-shooters are like the Avengers’ Quinjet. If it breaks down mid-air, we can't exactly call a tow truck, can we? That’s where an emergency fund comes in. It’s your Quinjet repair fund – a pot of money specifically for unexpected expenses. Think of it as your financial arc reactor, keeping you powered up when things go haywire.
dialogue.hint: Explain emergency funds using Avengers equipment needing maintenance; illustrate needing funds to fix equipment.

dialogue.text: Peter, about that photography gig I told you about… the Daily Bugle wants you to cover a gala next week. It pays really well, enough to probably cover half the web-shooter repair. But, Aunt May’s cat, Mittens, needs to see the vet. She’s acting weird and I don’t have enough saved right now. What should we do?
dialogue.hint: Present a moral dilemma: should Peter prioritize his work (to fund his emergency) or help his aunt with a pet emergency?

dialogue.text: Mr. Stark, MJ, I get it. I should have been prepared! I was so focused on earning money for the PlayStation 6 (and maybe impressing Liz Allen), I forgot that being a superhero comes with unexpected costs. Like, you know, Vulture shredding my tech!
dialogue.hint: Highlight the trade-off between saving for wants versus needs.

dialogue.text: Exactly, kid. Ideally, you want 3-6 months' worth of living expenses stashed away. Think rent, food, web-fluid, and maybe the occasional slice of pizza from Joe's. Even heroes need a safety net! It protects against the upside-down… financial upside-down, that is. It gives you time to plan, to breathe, and to find a *real* solution instead of taking the first offer that comes along.
dialogue.hint: Elaborate on the typical recommended size of an emergency fund and relate it to a popular sci-fi show.

dialogue.text: So, even if Vulture steals from Stark Industries and wrecks half of Manhattan, I can still fix my web-shooters and help Aunt May's cat… and *then* think about that PS6?
dialogue.hint: Reinforce the core concept and link it back to the initial problem.

characters.name: Spider-Man
characters.description: Peter Parker, wearing his classic red and blue Spider-Man suit. His mask is slightly torn, revealing a worried expression. He is kneeling, examining his damaged web-shooters. He looks young, perhaps 16-17, with a slightly scrawny build under the suit.

characters.name: Iron Man
characters.description: Tony Stark, in his iconic Iron Man suit, Mark LXXXV. The suit is slightly damaged from a battle. He’s hovering just above the ground, gesturing towards Spider-Man with a concerned expression. The arc reactor in his chest glows brightly.

characters.name: MJ
characters.description: Michelle Jones (MJ), standing next to Spider-Man. She’s wearing a sarcastic t-shirt, with a sketchpad and camera bag slung over her shoulder. She has a slightly worried expression, chewing on her lip. She’s wearing Converse sneakers and has messy, short brown hair.

backgrounds.name: Main location
backgrounds.description: A busy street in Manhattan. Taxis honk, people rush by. Stark Tower is visible in the background. A damaged bank building is partially visible, with caution tape around it, showcasing some financial element. A news ticker displays current stock prices.

backgrounds.name: Secondary location
backgrounds.description: Inside Peter's messy bedroom. Comic books and science projects are scattered around. A framed photo of Uncle Ben is on the desk. A piggy bank shaped like Spider-Man is visible on a shelf, mostly empty. A discarded web-shooter is lying on the floor.

visuals.financial_elements: Visualize the emergency fund as a glowing energy shield around Spider-Man, deflecting threats like a bill, a car repair, and a medical expense. Alternatively, a meter showing Spider-Man's financial health, ranging from 'Danger!' (empty) to 'Safe!' (full).

hooks.pop_culture: Iron Man mentions that an emergency fund will protect you from the 'financial upside-down', a reference to Stranger Things.
hooks.music: If Peter is feeling insecure about his financial situation, play a short, instrumental version of 'Anti-Hero' by Taylor Swift. A feeling of self-doubt and the irony of being a hero with financial problems.
